candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — support systems, client preferences and coping
candidate.educational_objective: Individualize family/support-person involvement according to the client's preferences, privacy needs and perioperative safety requirements.

options.A: Support each client's stated preference when clinically and operationally feasible, while protecting privacy and explaining any perioperative restrictions
options.B: Require family presence for both clients because support persons uniformly reduce anxiety in every surgical client
options.C: Exclude family for both clients because family presence has no psychosocial role in perioperative care
options.D: Allow family presence based only on the family's preference rather than the client's wishes

candidate.rationale: Perioperative psychosocial care is individualized. Family or other support persons may help some clients cope with anxiety, but not every client wants or benefits from the same arrangement. The nurse should center the capable adult client's preference, protect privacy, and follow clinical and facility restrictions rather than treating family presence as universally required or prohibited.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Perioperative nursing care and psychosocial support should be individualized to client preferences and values; family involvement is included when appropriate.
candidate.source_locator: Perioperative nursing advocacy: respect client rights and preferences; psychosocial responses of client/family should be addressed; care goals are individualized to client needs, values and beliefs
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
candidate.stem: Two adult clients are waiting for surgery. One asks to have a partner remain nearby for support; the other says they prefer privacy and do not want family present. Which nursing approach is best?
